earnings.title: Brookfield Asset Management Announces Record Second Quarter Results
highlights: Net income was $1.2 billion in the quarter and $3.1 billion over the last twelve months.
The board of directors of BAM declared a quarterly dividend of $0.5025 per share, payable on September 29, 2026, to shareholders of record as of the close of business on August 31, 2026.

quotes.text: We delivered a strong second quarter, with record fundraising of $77 billion, led by private equity, infrastructure, and credit. Fee-related earnings grew 20% to $808 million, and fee-bearing capital reached $672 billion, up 19% year-over-year, delivering performance above our long-term targets.

outlook: In July, we also committed approximately $3.0 billion to acquire the largest standalone energy storage business in North America expected to close later this year.
Deployment: We deployed $1.4 billion and signed an agreement to acquire the world’s largest air freight services provider, which is expected to close later this year.

items.heading: The trading price of the Class A Shares is subject to volatility due to market conditions and other factors and cannot be predicted.
Deficiencies in our public company financial reporting and disclosures could adversely impact our reputation.
Investors may find it difficult or impossible to effect service of process and enforce judgments against us, our directors and our executive officers.

We are subject to numerous laws, rules and regulatory requirements which may impact our business, including resulting in financial penalties, loss of business and/or damage to our reputation in instances of non-compliance.

Federal, state and foreign anti-bribery and corruption and trade sanctions laws and restrictions on foreign direct investment applicable to us and our managed assets create the potential for significant liabilities and penalties, the inability to complete transactions, imposition of significant costs and burdens, and reputational harm and we may also be subject to various governmental investigations.
Foreign exchange rate fluctuations could adversely impact our aggregate foreign currency exposure and hedging strategies may not be effective.
